newsitem.title: USA: Marathon profits jump 42 pct before items.
newsitem.headline: Marathon profits jump 42 pct before items.

text.p: USX-Marathon Group said Tuesday third quarter net income, excluding special items, was up 42 percent from 1995's September quarter.
The group said its operating income rose to $318 million from $173 million last year.

It said increases in worldwide liquid hydrocarbon and natural gas prices, along with higher natural gas volumes, resulted in upstream operating income of $222 million in the latest quarter, more than double last year's $103 million.
"These were the best quarterly upstream results in the past five years," Marathon said.
In the U.S., it said, the gains were offset by lower production at Ewing Bank Block 873 and other mature properties and from the 1995 sale of Illinois Basin production.

Domestic upstream operating income was $136 million, up from $72 million in 1995's third quarter. International exploration and production operating income rose to $86 million from $31 million helped by lower dry well expenses offset by lower UK production.

Refining, marketing and transportation operating income dropped to $35 million from $141 million a year ago even after a $15 million gain in the latest quarter from an adjustment to expected environmental remediation recoveries.
The drop in downstream results was mainly due to crude oil costs increasing faster than product prices, Marathon said.
Further restraining the latest quarter was a scheduled major turnaround last month at Marathon's 175,000 barrel per day Robinson, Ill., refinery.
